report:
The manuscript establishes an analytic obstruction for its frozen signature (7), subject to the caller-granted R. It does not establish that this signature is the complete, unchanged original P19.2 requirement. Consequently, the whole original is not settled by this argument. I found no essential mathematical defect in the constructed obstruction; the unresolved issue is the identification of the approximation request being disproved.

The precise established statement is: on X=P¹×Y, where Y is a compact Kähler complex two-torus with no nonzero integral (1,1) class, there is an actual finite-energy weak geodesic ray from 0, bounded at each finite time, whose normalized closed Legendre P-ceilings have positive mass and are not I-model on (-1,0]. No sequence of usual-datum maximal finite-energy rays from 0 can approximate these ceilings in d_S/V at any fixed λ∈(-1,0). This excludes the canonical model, positive flag, and canonical obstacle rays covered by R's model realization. It excludes every sequence in that category, rather than one construction.

The scope identification remains unproved. The original P19.2 text requests preservation of “all required energy, entropy and singularity data” and distinguishes I-equivalence from finer P-equivalence. It does not specify convergence at every fixed Legendre parameter in d_S, or identify the entire permitted approximation universe with canonical usual-datum maximal rays. Its residual discussion also includes regularization of rays attached to log-discrepancy models. The candidate instead uses a nonmaximal ray with usual datum zero. The instruction to freeze a signature does not itself establish that this particular universal arbitrary-ray signature is the unchanged atom. Thus the final comparison section's attribution of that precise requirement to the original is unsupported. This is an unresolved scope ambiguity, not evidence that a particular weaker approximation statement is true.

I independently opened the literal cited versions: [DX, published 2022 text](https://research.chalmers.se/publication/528300/file/528300_Fulltext.pdf), [DDNL, 1909.00839v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.00839v1), [DXZ, published 2025 text](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/49836), and [MP, 2409.06221v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.06221v2). Pertinent statement/proof units checked include DX Section 2.4 and Lemma 3.14; DDNL's ceiling, metric, monotone-limit, rooftop, diamond and lower-tail units through Theorem 5.6; and DXZ Section 2.2. I also opened the underlying [Darvas–Zhang 2208.08324v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2208.08324v3), Propositions 3.6 and 3.10 and Theorems 3.7 and 3.9, and the [published DDL envelope foundations](https://msp.org/apde/2018/11-8/apde-v11-n8-p06-s.pdf), including their applicable proofs. Neither author reading records nor historical verdicts were used as mathematical evidence. R's granted carrier, maximal-ray realization and entropy theorem were checked for application, not independently re-audited as new premises.

The I-model closedness argument works. For a nontrivial finite lower rooftop w of I-models u_i, every I-envelope competitor for w lies below every u_i, hence below w; w is itself admissible. Therefore w is I-model. Mass continuity gives a common positive lower mass bound for a d_S-convergent sequence approaching a positive-mass target. DDNL's rapidly convergent subsequence construction supplies nontrivial finite rooftops and positive lower tails. The finite rooftops are I-model; their decreasing limits remain I-model; the increasing almost-everywhere limit is I-model because the target is a positive-mass P-model. This retains d_S convergence as the hypothesis. It does not replace it with L¹ convergence or assert completeness without a mass lower bound. DDNL v1 uses C-models in several units; C=P at positive mass supplies the necessary identification.

The nonprojective maximality bridge also works. First, genuine Legendre levels of an actual geodesic from 0 are P-model. One can verify this directly: if v≤0 and v≤χ_λ+C, then v+λs−Cs/T is an admissible subgeodesic competitor on [0,T]. Geodesic comparison gives v+λs−Cs/T≤U_s. Let T increase, then take the infimum over s, to obtain v≤χ_λ. This proves the required envelope equality without a polarization. Interior levels have positive mass: increasing levels approach the full-mass reference at −∞, and concavity with another genuine level propagates positivity to every interior parameter.

For the local Gauss calculation, write v=(a/b)ord_E and realize its extension by normal weights a,b. With coefficients measured against log|s|², the summand χ_λ−λlog|τ|² has coefficient a·ν_E(χ_λ)−bλ. Dividing its negative by b gives λ−ν_v(χ_λ). After adding a bounded local background, the family is locally uniformly upper bounded. The supremum Lelong rule applies on the modification; a countable determining family permits a common generic point. Hence W^NA(v)=sup_{λ<λ+}(λ−ν_v(χ_λ)), with no extra squared-log factor. The strict central component gives the same formula for the trivial valuation.

I-maximization preserves every interior multiplier ideal and therefore every relevant divisorial coefficient. Its closed test curve is relative to P_I[0]=0. Its masses lie between the old masses and 1, so its negative mass-defect integral remains finite. Its inverse transform is consequently a genuine finite-energy weak geodesic competitor W≥U. The Gauss calculation and R's divisorial determination give equality of actual usual data on the full supported carrier. Usual maximality then forces U=W, and Legendre injectivity forces every interior level to be I-model. At a genuine cutoff, the decreasing left limit is I-model as well: its I-envelope lies below every preceding I-model level and therefore below their limit. This argument does not require positive cutoff mass. No projective density theorem from DX's later sections, DXZ Section 3.1, or MP's comparison sketch is used.

The diffuse-polar construction checks out. The nested disjoint cylinders have Bernoulli mass 2^(-m), so the measure is nonatomic. The Green kernel is nonpositive and uniformly integrable against smooth area; reverse Fatou gives upper semicontinuity, Fubini gives L¹, and distributional differentiation gives dd^c h=ν−ω_C. At a point of K, its cylinder contributes at most 2^(-m)log(4r_m²), tending to −∞ because r_m=exp(−4^m). Off K the kernel is locally uniformly finite. Thus the pole set is exactly K, making K polar and area-null.

Atomlessness gives uniform small-ball masses. For any exponent A>0, choose a doubled ball of mass m<1/A. The far contribution is bounded below, and Jensen bounds e^(−Ah) by an average of |z−b|^(−2Am). The area integrals are uniformly finite because Am<1. This proves local integrability for every coefficient. For ch, its current is (1−c)ω_C+cν; the nonpluripolar restriction removes precisely the measure supported on K, giving mass 1−c. The P-envelope q_c preserves that mass, is idempotent at positive mass, and satisfies q_c≥ch. Its multiplier ideals are therefore trivial, P_I[q_c]=0, and q_c≠0.

The torus argument is sufficient. Integral degree-two classes on R⁴/Z⁴ have constant alternating representatives. Translation averaging preserves type and cohomology, so an integral class is (1,1) precisely when its constant representative is J-invariant. For each nonzero integral alternating form, the displayed family of oriented complex structures violates invariance for some choice of st. Its invariant locus is therefore a proper closed analytic subset with empty interior. Baire avoids the countable union. Constant positive Hermitian forms provide Kähler forms. An ample bundle would contradict the absence of integral (1,1) classes. Restricting to Y shows both that X is nonprojective and that [ω] cannot be proportional to a line-bundle class.

The product-envelope identity is exact at each finite rooftop: pullback supplies one inequality, while restriction of any competitor to C×{y} supplies the other, including identically −∞ restrictions. The increasing regularized limit preserves this equality. Product Fubini proves trivial multiplier ideals. Writing B=∫_Y ω_Y² gives V=3B. In the truncated products, the curve factor occurs with multiplicities k and 3−k; two curve factors vanish. Removing the pole set loses no smooth area. The integral is therefore (3−kc)B, and M_k=1−kc/3, including M_0=1 and M_3=1−c. No singular-level mass is converted into a probability measure.

The raw test curve is decreasing, concave and closed, including its extended values on K. P-maximization and pullback preserve these properties. At λ=0, the decreasing left limit dominates q_c0, is P-model, and has mass 1−c0>0. Equal positive mass for this ordered pair forces equality, so the endpoint is genuine and exactly q_c0. Below and at −1 the levels are 0; above 0 they are identically −∞. There are no raw-zero target levels.

The Ross–Witt Nyström transform gives the actual weak geodesic. The −1 level and nonpositive ceilings imply −t≤U_t≤0. These bounds give strong convergence to 0 at the start and extend the finite-interval geodesic property to intervals beginning at zero. The normalized energy formula yields E(U_t)/t=−c0/2. All genuine levels have trivial ideals, hence zero divisorial coefficients; the calibrated Gauss supremum is zero. R extends this as the zero usual datum on the whole carrier. Its maximalization from 0 is stationary. The nonzero energy defect proves nonmaximality, and R, applied in its fixed smooth compact-Kähler domain with H(0)=0, gives entropy slope +∞.

Finally, any approximating maximal ray's level is either interior and I-model, a genuine cutoff and I-model, or identically −∞ and inadmissible. A genuine zero-mass level cannot approach the positive target mass. Applying the established positive-mass d_S-closedness would make the target I-model, contradicting its I-envelope zero and its mass below one. Thus the frozen obstruction is universal within the stated category.

Harmless wording corrections: “bounded ray” should explicitly mean bounded at each finite time, not uniformly bounded for all t; and the DDNL C/P terminology must retain its positive-mass qualification. Establishing that equation (7) and the canonical maximal-ray category are the full original P19.2 specification would require an additional scope argument. It cannot be supplied as a wording correction.

premises: DX Proposition 2.18: on a compact Kähler manifold with smooth pseudoeffective form θ, P_I[u] is an admissible θ-psh P-model, dominates P[u], has the same multiplier ideals as u at every positive coefficient, and satisfies P_I[P_I[u]]=P_I[u].

DX Theorem 2.13 and Corollary 2.16: for θ-psh potentials on a compact Kähler manifold with smooth pseudoeffective θ, inclusion of all multiplier ideals is equivalent to reverse inequality of pulled-back Lelong numbers at all points of every smooth projective modification; equality is equivalent to equality of these numbers.

DX Lemma 2.21: for normalized P-model potentials in a fixed smooth pseudoeffective class on a compact Kähler manifold, a decreasing I-model sequence with a P-model limit retains I-modelness; an increasing almost-everywhere I-model sequence with a positive-mass P-model limit also retains I-modelness.

DX Lemma 3.14: on any complex manifold, the Lelong number of the upper-semicontinuous regularization of the supremum of a nonempty nonpositive psh family is the infimum of the members' Lelong numbers.

DDNL Lemma 3.4, Proposition 3.5 and Lemma 3.7: for its fixed-Kähler-class singularity distance on a compact Kähler n-fold, ordered types satisfy d_S/V=Σ_k(M_k(v)−M_k(u))/(n+1); for arbitrary types, |M_k(u)−M_k(v)|≤C_n d_S/V.

DDNL Theorem 5.6: in a big class on a compact Kähler manifold, d_S-convergent normalized P-models with uniformly positive top mass have a subsequence whose nontrivial finite lower rooftops decrease to positive-mass P-model tails, increasing almost everywhere to the normalized P-model limit.

DDNL Proposition 2.6, Corollary 4.7 and Proposition 4.8: in a big class on a compact Kähler manifold, C=P at positive mass; a decreasing C-model sequence with top mass at least δ>0 has a C-model limit and convergent mixed masses against the minimal-singularity reference.

DDL Section 3B and Theorem 3.12: on a compact Kähler manifold with smooth big θ, a normalized θ-psh potential and its P-envelope have equal nonpluripolar top mass; if that mass is positive, P[P[u]]=P[u].
DDL Theorem 3.14: in a big class on a compact Kähler manifold, for θ-psh u≤φ+C with φ of positive top mass, equality of their nonpluripolar top masses is equivalent to P[u]=P[φ].

DDL Theorems 2.3–2.4 and Remark 2.5: for smooth closed big forms on a compact Kähler manifold, mixed nonpluripolar masses increase when potentials become less singular and converge along increasing almost-everywhere sequences.

DXZ Theorem 2.6: in a Kähler class on a connected compact Kähler manifold, with reference 0, closed maximal test curves and weak geodesic rays are inverse Legendre transforms. Finite energy is characterized by λ+ +∫_{−∞}^{λ+}(M_n(χ_λ)−1)dλ>−∞, and this expression equals the ray's normalized energy slope, with dd^c=i∂∂bar/(2π) and squared-log time.

DXZ Section 2.2 maximization constructions: for a test curve in a Kähler class on a connected compact Kähler manifold, with limit 0 at −∞ and finite cutoff, replacing interior levels by P-envelopes or I-envelopes, taking the decreasing left limit at the cutoff, and assigning −∞ above it produces a closed maximal or I-maximal test curve, respectively, again relative to 0.
